_comment: WHAT THIS RIG MEASURED IN THIS ROOM, ON THIS DAY. The only file of the three
that is expected to change between the load-in and the doors, and again the
next morning after somebody knocks a head.
Because it is separate and timestamped, an overnight nudge is a DIFF against
last night rather than a from-scratch re-aim -- which is the whole point of
ball_dmx: aim the head at the mirror ball by hand and record the two 0-255
readings, (pan, tilt). Everything else the engine does is a geometric offset
from that one verified point, so this is THE calibration step. A head left
null falls back to the assumed mounting model, which is markedly worse.
The readings are mount-mode specific -- a bench 'table' reading and a real
'venue' reading calibrate two physically different transforms and are not
interchangeable. These are venue readings, matching rig.json's mount_mode.
pan_invert/tilt_invert describe the FIXTURE's own DMX-to-rotation wiring.
In 'venue' the base is tipped on its side so Pan carries ELEVATION, which is
why heads 2 and 4 differ: they are mounted mirrored from their neighbours,
so their up/down handedness is flipped. A per-head difference is legitimate
on the elevation channel and NOT on the bearing channel -- a mixed bearing
invert breaks every pose that aims one head relative to another.
source: ported from events/despacio/despacio_config.json, the calibration the show ran on
